title: Where the Settlement Clock Starts on an Auto Loan Being Paid in Full
content:
The date from which the settlement clock runs, when a loan of the Auto Loans line is settled in full, turns on two readings of the borrower's Personal Checking account: whether they hold an active checking account whose posted balance is at least the fee-waiver daily balance its tier publishes, and whether at least 2 recurring deposits have posted to that account in the last three months.

- Where both hold, the clock runs from the date the most recent entry posted to the loan.
- Where exactly one of those two holds, the clock runs from the date the installment then due falls on.
- Where neither of them holds, the clock runs from the date of the last payment credited to the loan.

## The three anchors on one loan

Take a loan whose most recent entry of any kind posted 4 days ago, whose installment then due falls on a date 12 days ago, and whose last credited payment was 30 days ago. The first anchor gives a span of 4 days, the second 12 and the third 30.

The most recent entry posted to the loan is the latest entry of any kind on its activity, a charge or a correction as readily as a payment, which is why the first anchor is usually the shortest span of the three.

## Where the two readings come from

The balance reading compares the posted balance on the borrower's active account in the Personal Checking line against the fee-waiver daily balance published for that account's tier. The deposit reading counts recurring deposits posted to that same account over the three months ending on the day of the settlement; exactly 2 meets the reading and 1 does not.
